text:
samira_support: FYI customer #8421 opened an escalation — p99 for rwd-13b requests jumped from ~420ms -> ~1.1s after the evening config roll. They say throughput is fine but tail latency is killing UX.
lucas_eng: ack — any idea which change landed in the roll?
devon_infra: the deploy notes show a quant profile swap at 02:12 UTC: `quant_profile: int8_aggressive_v2` applied to rwd-13b canary group (10%).
samira_support: timeline from customer: spike started ~02:18 and persisted; they were routed to canary model variants.
jen_sre: grabbing traces + flamegraphs now. can you paste grafana link? (or ping me the org id)
samira_support: grafana: https://grafana.redwood/exp/8421/dash?panel=p99_latency (customer-facing link scrubbed) — p95 also crept up ~60%.
jen_sre: quick look at traces — lots of nuclear loops in attention kernel on certain sequence lengths (>=1024). KV cache miss ratio also higher on canary.
arman_ml: that matches a hypothesis: int8_aggressive_v2 changed per-layer quant scale heuristics; for long sequences it increases recompute and dequant ops which can amplify tail latency.
lucas_eng: can we reproduce in staging? devon, do we have a staging canary with same profile?
devon_infra: yes, staging has an env with int8_aggressive_v2. I'll run a short cURL load to measure p99.
devon_infra: (log) `wrk -t4 -c50 -d30s --latency http://staging-models/rwd-13b/generate` -> p50 360ms, p95 540ms, p99 1.03s — matches production-ish.
jen_sre: repro steps for SRE/infra: 1) deploy staging with `quant_profile=int8_aggressive_v2` 2) run `wrk` or our internal `loadtest` with sequences 512/1024 and batch sizes 1..8, measure p95/p99 3) collect GPU sysstats `nvidia-smi dmon` and runtime traces.
arman_ml: immediate mitigation options: a) rollback canary to previous profile (int8_balanced_v1) b) enable fallback to fp16 for `seq_len>512` c) reduce canary weight to 0% while we investigate d) adjust quant config to disable per-layer aggressive re-scaling.
samira_support: customer asks for a hot fix — what can we offer right now? they want minimal change that gets tail under 600ms.
lucas_eng: quickest is to flip the canary weight to 0% (effectively rollback) — this requires infra approval but should be <5m. Second-fastest is enabling model-level fp16 fallback for long sequences.
devon_infra: issuing command to set canary=0% now: `rwctl rollout update rwd-13b --canary-weight 0` — rolling.
ops-bot: deploybot: rollback applied for rwd-13b — canary weight -> 0% by devon_infra at 02:34 UTC.
samira_support: customer confirms improved latency ~-> p99 580ms after rollback, still monitoring. They appreciate the quick action :thumbsup:
jen_sre: follow-up actions: - run deterministic perf tests comparing int8_aggressive_v2 vs int8_balanced_v1 across seq lens 128/512/1024 - add regression alert for p99 delta > 30% after quant profile changes - add a check in rollout pipeline to run a short latency microbenchmark before increasing canary weight above 5%.
arman_ml: for root cause: I'll run per-layer activation histograms and calibration logs; suspect outlier layers where scale quantization triggers expensive dequant/requant sequences. Will push a patch to profile heuristics if confirmed.
lucas_eng: I'll open ENG ticket ENG-PLAT-1287 with repro artifacts, wrk scripts, and perf traces. Assign to arman_ml + devon_infra + jen_sre. ETA initial triage 24h.
samira_support: adding to the customer case: hot rollback applied, mitigation steps listed, we will provide ETA for a permanent fix. Will keep them updated hourly until resolved.
jen_sre: tagging for postmortem if this hits SLA next week. Also we should consider adding a fallback rule in routing: if p99 exceeds threshold, autoswitch to fp16 variant automatically.
samira_support: thanks all — leaving thread open until ENG ticket updates. :heart:
